questions.q: When the service desk first receives the checkout discount error, what should happen first?
options: Wait to see if it recurs before taking any action
Open a problem record before anything else is logged
Log it as an incident and triage it by impact and urgency
Immediately submit an emergency change to patch the code
questions.explain: The first response to any disruption is incident management: log it and triage based on impact and urgency, not root-cause investigation.

questions.q: Why does restarting the microservice count as a legitimate incident resolution, even though nobody yet knows why it keeps crashing?
options: Incident management's job is restoring normal service operation, not diagnosing root cause
Incident management is only allowed to resolve incidents that never recur
It doesn't count as a resolution unless the root cause is also found
Restarting a service is always classified as a change, not an incident fix
questions.explain: Incident management is judged on restoring service quickly; root cause investigation is explicitly a separate practice's responsibility.

questions.q: Why does the fourth occurrence of the identical symptom in a month trigger a problem investigation?
options: A recurring pattern across multiple incidents is a classic trigger for problem identification, rather than one isolated incident
It means the previous three restarts were not valid incident resolutions
A fourth occurrence automatically becomes a major incident
Problem records are opened automatically after every single incident
questions.explain: A single incident rarely proves a problem exists; a repeating pattern is exactly the signal problem identification watches for.

questions.q: Why is the memory-leak fix handled as a normal change rather than an emergency change in this scenario?
options: The fix cannot be implemented at all until a major incident occurs
Normal changes never require any authorization
Emergency changes are reserved only for standard changes
A working workaround already exists and no outage is actively happening, so there's time for full risk assessment and scheduling
questions.explain: Emergency changes are for fixes that can't wait; since the restart workaround keeps the business running, this fix can go through full normal-change evaluation.

questions.q: What finally allows the known error record to be closed in this scenario?
options: The fourth incident is resolved with a restart
The patched change deploys successfully and monitoring confirms the incident stops recurring
The problem is identified and root cause is documented
The change advisory board approves the deployment window
questions.explain: A known error closes once its permanent fix is implemented and verified to actually stop the recurring incidents — not merely once it's approved or diagnosed.
